title: Depth in a short exact sequence of nonzero finite modules over a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], i.e. a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $0\to N'\to N\to N''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] in which $N'$, $N$, $N''$ are nonzero finite $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $\operatorname{depth}$ for the depth $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], with values in $\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, $\infty-1=\infty$ and $\infty+1=\infty$. Then (1) $\operatorname{depth}(N)\ge\min\{\operatorname{depth}(N'),\operatorname{depth}(N'')\}$; (2) $\operatorname{depth}(N'')\ge\min\{\operatorname{depth}(N),\operatorname{depth}(N')-1\}$; (3) $\operatorname{depth}(N')\ge\min\{\operatorname{depth}(N),\operatorname{depth}(N'')+1\}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LX (lemma-depth-in-ses, lines 17904-17916), proof lines 17918-17936 (Ext characterization of depth, Lemma Tag 00LW lemma-depth-ext line 17863, and the long exact Ext sequence). proof.text: (Depth by vanishing of Ext.) Put $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. Each of $N'$, $N$, $N''$ is a nonzero finite module over the Noetherian local ring $R$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-ext] (Stacks 00LW) its depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] is a finite integer $\ge0$ equal to the smallest $i\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,-)\neq0$, Ext as in [def-pc-ext]. Consequently, for $X\in\{N',N,N''\}$ and every integer $n$: $\operatorname{depth}(X)\ge n$ if and only if $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,X)=0$ for all integers $0\le i<n$ (if $\operatorname{depth}(X)\ge n$, every $i<n$ is below the smallest index of a nonzero Ext; conversely, if all $\operatorname{Ext}^i$ with $i<n$ vanish, the smallest index of a nonzero Ext is $\ge n$; for $n\le0$ both sides hold). In particular all depths in the statement are integers, so the conventions $\infty\pm1=\infty$ are not needed, and in (2) the bound $\operatorname{depth}(N')-1$ may be $-1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LX proof ("Use the characterization of depth using the Ext groups, see Lemma 00LW"), lines 17918-17920

proof.text: (The long exact sequence.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-second-variable] (Stacks 00LU) to $M=\kappa$ and the short exact sequence $0\to N'\xrightarrow{u}N\xrightarrow{v}N''\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: for every $i\ge0$ the sequences (a) $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N')\xrightarrow{u_*}\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N)\xrightarrow{v_*}\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N'')$, (b) $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N)\xrightarrow{v_*}\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N'')\xrightarrow{\delta^i}\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_R(\kappa,N')$, (c) $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(\kappa,N'')\xrightarrow{\delta^i}\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_R(\kappa,N')\xrightarrow{u_*}\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_R(\kappa,N)$ are exact at the middle term, and (c$_0$) $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,N')\xrightarrow{u_*}\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,N)$ is exact, i.e. $u_*$ is injective in degree $0$. In an exact sequence $A\to B\to C$ of abelian groups with $A=0$ and $C=0$ one has $B=0$ (the kernel of $B\to C$ is all of $B$ and equals the image of $A$, which is $0$); likewise $B=0$ when $B\to C$ is injective and $C=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LX proof (the long exact cohomology sequence from Lemma 00LU), lines 17920-17935

proof.text: (Part (1).) Let $n=\min\{\operatorname{depth}(N'),\operatorname{depth}(N'')\}$ and $0\le i<n$. Then $i<\operatorname{depth}(N')$ and $i<\operatorname{depth}(N'')$, so $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N')=0$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N'')=0$ by Step 1, and the exact sequence (a) of Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N)=0$. By Step 1 again, $\operatorname{depth}(N)\ge n$.

(Part (2).) Let $n=\min\{\operatorname{depth}(N),\operatorname{depth}(N')-1\}$ and $0\le i<n$ (if $n\le0$ there is nothing to prove, depths being $\ge0$). Then $i<\operatorname{depth}(N)$ and $i+1<\operatorname{depth}(N')$, so $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N)=0$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_R(\kappa,N')=0$ by Step 1, and the exact sequence (b) of Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N'')=0$. By Step 1, $\operatorname{depth}(N'')\ge n$.

(Part (3).) Let $n=\min\{\operatorname{depth}(N),\operatorname{depth}(N'')+1\}$ and $0\le i<n$. Then $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N)=0$ by Step 1 since $i<\operatorname{depth}(N)$. If $i=0$, (c$_0$) of Step 2 makes $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,N')\to\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,N)=0$ injective, so $\operatorname{Ext}^0_R(\kappa,N')=0$. If $i\ge1$, then $i-1<\operatorname{depth}(N'')$, so $\operatorname{Ext}^{i-1}_R(\kappa,N'')=0$ by Step 1, and the exact sequence (c) of Step 2 with index $i-1$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{i-1}_R(\kappa,N'')\to\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N')\to\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N)$, gives $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,N')=0$. By Step 1, $\operatorname{depth}(N')\ge n$.
